title: The Hidden Fragility of GNNs: How Graph Structure Amplifies Numerical Errors

problem.claim: GNNs are unusually fragile under mixed-precision training, with graph structure amplifying numerical errors.

gap.claim: Existing naive approaches that enforce neighbor alignment can reduce numerical fragility by destroying discriminative representation diversity.

contributions.claim: The paper attributes GNN numerical fragility to catastrophic cancellation during neighborhood aggregation, especially when neighboring embeddings point in opposite directions.
The paper formalizes cancellation using a cancellation ratio and relates it to graph topology, including heterophily, node degree, and network depth.
The paper proposes Aggregation-Aware Representation Learning (AARL) to produce numerically stable, cancellation-resistant representations while preserving expressiveness and representation diversity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on diverse benchmarks reportedly show that AARL substantially improves training stability under low precision while preserving or improving classification accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs fail more often than MLPs or CNNs under mixed-precision training.
Vulnerability is associated with graph structure, particularly heterophily and high-degree nodes.
Catastrophic cancellation during neighborhood aggregation amplifies floating-point errors.
A cancellation ratio is used to connect numerical instability with graph topology.
AARL is proposed and is reported to improve low-precision stability without harming classification accuracy.

source_observation.claim: Neighborhood aggregation can become numerically unstable when neighboring representations point in opposite directions.

interpretation.claim: Representation aggregation should account for cancellation risk, not only semantic alignment or expressiveness.

application.claim: For low-precision graph models, evaluate topology-aware aggregation stability alongside task accuracy.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach generalizes beyond the reported graph benchmarks or precision settings.

unknowns: The cancellation ratio symbol and its precise definition are not supplied.
The abstract does not specify benchmark datasets, precision formats, failure rates, or quantitative effect sizes.
The abstract does not provide proof details or independent verification of the reported results.
